headline: Approved asking the mayor to close the Main Library from 5:00 to 8:00 p.m. on September 30, 2026 for an author event.
summary: The meeting covered library statistics, the summer reading program, the Centennial Fund, and the Laptop Connect program. The board approved the July 6, 2026 minutes and asked the mayor to close the Main Library for an author event on September 30, 2026.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the July 6, 2026 Regular Meeting, all in favor.

decision_titles: Minutes of the July 6, 2026 Regular Meeting
Closing Main Library for Allegra Goodman event
plain_text:
1 
 
MEETING MINUTES OF THE BOARD OF LIBRARY DIRECTORS 
 
MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 14, 2026 
 
Bristol Public Library, 5 High Street, Bristol, CT 06010 
 
ATTENDEES: Valina Carpenter, Eric Frenette, Nicholas Jakubowski, 
Elizabeth Kanachovski, Andrea Kapchensky, Kimberly Ploszaj (Zoom), 
Danielle Rivard (Zoom), Pina Salvatore, and Betty Talmadge. 
Library Director Deborah Prozzo and Assistant Library Director Scott 
Stanton. 
 
Absent: City Council Liaison Steve Seymour. 
 
Item 1– Call to Order 
  
Chairperson Salvatore called the meeting to order at 6:31 p.m. 
Item 2- Public Participation 
  
None. 
Item 3- Approval of Minutes 
  
Director Talmadge MOVED to approve the Minutes of the July 6, 
2026 Regular Meeting. Seconded by Director Kanachovski. All in 
favor. None opposed. Motion passed. 
Item 4- Communications 
   
Library Director Prozzo received a card from a patron thanking 
us for the services we provide to the community. In particular, 
she emphasized her appreciation for the computer lab and Don 
Smith who’s been invaluable. They are far from tech-savvy and 
Don has provided a lot of assistance. The card says, “Best 
public library ever.” 
Item 5- Reports and Committee Reports 
 
a. Finance Committee 
 
No Report. 
b. Property Committee 
 
No Report. 
c. Policy Committee 
 
No Report. 
d. Strategic Planning Committee 
 
No Report.
2 
 
e. Library Director’s Report 
 
1) June 2026, FY2026 & July 2026 Statistics 
 
We had a very strong finish to the fiscal year 2026. The library 
circulated 262,706 items, we had 176,128 patron visits, we 
hosted almost 1,500 programs, and we had over 50,000 people of 
all ages in attendance. There were 105,000 Wi-Fi sessions and 
588,000 website visits. We had 2,182 new cardholders and we 
answered more than 27,000 questions. 
In July, we had a little decrease in circulation, but our 
program offerings increased by 8%, patron registrations 
increased by 6%, and patron visits increased by 3%. 
2) Year-to-Date Budget 
 
We are only 2 months into the new fiscal year, so there really 
isn’t much to report at this time. We are still waiting for the 
trust funds to carry over. Revenue is up. The detailed report 
for all of our trust funds shows what we’ve spent to date on 
book purchases and programming. 
There’s over $50,000 in the Centennial Fund interest account and 
$1,050 in the Centennial Fund contribution account (checks and 
cash). We discovered that we will have to do a deposit to move 
online donations made via Stripe into a contribution account. 
The Centennial Fund has three revenue accounts and one 
expenditure account. If the Library Board wants to move money 
from a revenue account into the expenditure account, Debbie will 
do the appropriation paperwork for the Board of Finance. 
3) Summer Reading 
 
We had a very successful summer reading program at both 
locations. The library was very busy. Thank you to the Friends 
of the Library for supporting us financially with very nice 
prizes and to the Hospitality Committee for providing 
refreshments and hospitality at many of the events. 
We ended the summer with a huge children’s author event. We 
hosted Lucky Diaz, who is Mexican-American and came from Los 
Angeles. He put on a wonderful performance and was very gracious 
and patient. He spent a lot of time with the individual families 
and signed copies of his book, which the children received for 
free. RJ Julia gave us a bulk discount. Over 180 children and 
adults attended. Thanks to the Friends, the lunch line moved 
along smoothly. Manross Trust Funds were used for this great 
community event. We did not have to pay for travel because Lucky 
was already here on the East Coast. Both the Children’s 
Department and the Manross Memorial Library offered related 
programming to support the event and prepare the attendees.
3 
 
4) Allegra Goodman Author Event 
 
Allegra Goodman will be traveling from Massachusetts, to New 
York, and then to Connecticut. She will give a presentation here 
at the Main Library on Wednesday, September 30, 2026. We are 
taking advantage of a great opportunity to host an author of 
that caliber at that price point. Due to limited parking and the 
inability to rely on Funks for additional parking, I am asking 
the Library Board to support me in asking the mayor if we could 
close the Main Library from 5:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. in order to 
accommodate all of the attendees. Right now, we have about 120 
people signed up for tickets and 92-96 parking spots. We will 
ask attendees to carpool and the employees will park elsewhere. 
Staff working that night would man the phones for regular 
library business, assist with parking, etc. Manross Library 
would remain open.  
Director Rivard MOVED to request approval from the mayor to 
close the Main Library from 5:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. on September 
30, 2026 for the Allegra Goodman event. Seconded by Director 
Ploszaj. All in favor. None opposed. Motion passed. 
5) Annual State Report 
The annual state report is due on October 1st, but I completed it 
and submitted it on August 12th. By participating, we will get 
money back from the state. I have a copy on file if anyone would 
like to see it. 
6) National Friends of the Library Week 
We will be celebrating National Friends of the Library Week 
which is October 18 – 24. We are planning to have either a 
breakfast or a luncheon here to recognize the Friends and all 
their hard work this past year. 
7) Laptop Connect Library 
We are a Laptop Connect library. We are participating in a 
program sponsored by the State Library and the DEEP which will 
allow us to bring 97 free laptops to our community. The state 
requires participants to have a valid library card in their 
town. You must be at least 18 years old. You must also be in one 
of the following assistance programs: SNAP, Medicare, Husky, CT 
Energy Assistance Program, or Low-Income Energy Assistance 
Program. We are currently taking names of people who are 
interested. During intake, we will meet with the individuals to 
make sure they are eligible. After attending a digital training 
session with Don Smith in the computer lab, they could then 
check out a computer, which comes with a small briefcase, for a 
5-year loan period. The expectation is that we will not see the 
computers again. Tech support and service will be provided via a 
1-800 number. We have to maintain the inventory. The state does 
not want to know who has the computers, just that they were
4 
 
distributed according to the rules. Participants would need to 
have their own wi-fi at home. Spread the word. Not all libraries 
chose to participate. 
f. City Council Liaison Report 
 
No Report. 
g. Friends of the Library 
 
Chairperson Salvatore reported the following: 
The 21st Annual National Friends of the Libraries Week is October 
18th through the 24th. The celebration offers a two-fold 
opportunity to celebrate the Friends. The Friends can use the 
time to raise awareness of their group in the community and to 
promote membership. It’s also an opportunity for the library and 
Library Board to recognize the Friends for their help and 
support. On behalf of the Library Board, we thank the Friends of 
the Bristol Public Library for their hard work, fundraising, 
advocacy, and dedication to making our community a better place. 
The Friends’ volunteers make our libraries special. They run the 
bookstore, attend special events like the Farmers’ Market, 
provide hospitality, etc. We’re very fortunate to have a very 
active and committed Friends group. 
The Friends now have a Facebook page. We invite you to follow 
“Friends of the Bristol CT Library” to learn about upcoming 
events. Holly works hard as the Friends’ Publicity Chair. 
The Friends offer sponsorships throughout the year whereby staff 
can apply for funds to help support special projects or 
equipment. The applications are subject to review and approval 
by the Friends’ Sponsorship Committee. For example, the Friends 
are sponsoring the Young Adult Junk Journaling Program on 
September 21st. 
Recently, two members of the Friends Board have partnered with 
the Children’s Department to set up a Friends table at certain 
children’s events. They sell children’s and youth books in good 
condition and promote the Friends group. They have attended two 
children’s events so far and plan to do more in the future. 
Preparations are underway for the Holiday Lobby Book Sale which 
will take place at both libraries in December. 
The Friends helped celebrate the close of the summer reading 
program with funding for refreshments and prizes. 
In July and August, the Friends held their first annual Dollar 
Days sales in the Friends Café on the second floor. Deep 
discounts were offered on books, DVDs, and CDs. 
The Friends have been involved in a lot of community activities. 
On August 18th, they partnered with the library at the Pencil
5 
 
Hunt at Muzzy Field, which was organized by Parks and Rec. The 
library solicited new library cards and the Friends gave away 
good quality children’s books for free. It was also an 
opportunity for the Friends to promote themselves. The total 
number of books distributed for all community events was 
approximately 260. 
The Friends attended the Farmers’ Market on September 12th along 
with library staff. Rose Ann reports that the gift card raffles 
and sale of low-cost books were very successful this summer. 
h. Community Engagement Committee 
 
Director Kanachovski confirmed that the Lucky Diaz event was a 
success and that the Allegra Goodman event will be held at the 
end of September.  
i. Centennial Ad-hoc Committee 
Director Carpenter reported that the committee met after Betty, 
Beth, and Debbie did quite a bit of research. They reviewed many 
documents to look at the history and intent of the fund which 
was started in 1992. There seemed to be a hole in some of the 
information from 1992 to 1995. We are trying to piece the puzzle 
together with meeting minutes from the actual committee, the 
Library Board, and the City Council. One of the questions is 
whether this was a permanent endowment or a city account? On 
September 11, 1995, the Library Board put the money in an 
endowment fund and wanted to dissolve the committee. Library 
Director Prozzo explained that we have a copy of the Library 
Board’s resolution to establish the fund but no evidence that 
the City Council actually took action on that. The City Clerk 
looked at records from 1994 to 1997 and could not find City 
Council meeting minutes that talked about the resolution. 
Library Director Prozzo offered to contact Corp Council since 
they drew up the original resolution and might have something on 
file that indicates that it did go through the City Council. 
Director Kapchensky stated that if it’s an endowment fund, there 
are lots of restrictions regarding how the money can be used. 
Library Director Prozzo explained that the fund, as it stands 
with the city right now, does not use the word “endowment.” We 
have no problem accessing the money which is in an expenditure 
account. We’ve used it twice for various projects. We’re earning 
interest, getting contributions, and the donate button is live 
on the website. Director Carpenter noted that during the 
Centennial Ad-hoc Committee’s informational meeting, there was 
some discussion about perhaps moving the fund to Main Street 
Community Foundation. 
 
Item 6- Old Business 
 
None.
6 
 
Item 7- New Business 
 
Director Kanachovski inquired about having one Library Board 
meeting a year at the Manross Library, which had been done prior 
to Covid. Discussion followed regarding meeting room 
availability at Manross and the 2027 Library Board meeting 
schedule.  
Library Director Prozzo reported that September is National 
Library Card Sign-up Month. We are encouraging all Bristol 
residents to get a free Bristol Library card, which opens the 
door to many resources, including digital databases. We will be 
out in the community on Thursday morning promoting library cards 
and library services at the Senior Center Health Fair. Director 
Frenette suggested going to St. Joseph School one day to do 
sign-ups and Director Rivard offered to bring flyers to the 
various schools. Assistant Library Director Stanton provided 
Chairperson Salvatore with Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu’s 
Proclamation regarding Library Card Sign-up Month which was 
established in 1987. Chairperson Salvatore read part of the 
Proclamation aloud. It is celebrated every September to mark the 
beginning of the school year and to emphasize the value of 
public libraries.  
Item 8- Adjournment 
 
There being no further business, Director Kapchensky made a 
MOTION to adjourn the meeting at 7:25 p.m. Seconded by Director 
Carpenter. All present voted in favor and the meeting adjourned. 
 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
Ruth Vontell 
 
This meeting was digitally recorded.
